points.description: States that hydroxide ions (OH-) / alkalinity are consumed or react (bond/combine) with the coagulant or its hydrolysis products (metal ions/molecules) during coagulation.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only says alkalinity is consumed/reacts with the coagulant without naming OH- (or bicarbonate/hydroxide) as the species.

points.description: States that this leaves/releases more H+ (H+ concentration increases), which lowers the pH.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only says pH decreases or water becomes acidic without linking to H+ increase.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both ideas: OH- (alkalinity) is used up by reacting with the coagulant, and H+ rises so pH falls. Give part marks where an idea is vague, e.g. only 'pH drops' or only 'alkalinity reacts with coagulant'. Give no marks for unrelated causes such as dilution, temperature or settling of sludge.
